rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The bāʾ in “bihi” is extra, so the phrase means that they listen to it.
rows.anchor: قيل: الباء زائدة في قوله «به» أي يستمعونه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: They listened to the Prophet recite the Qur’an, then withdrew and called him a magician and bewitched.
rows.anchor: هو ساحر ومسحور كما أخبر الله تعالى به عنهم قاله قتادة وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their being “in private counsel” means they whispered together about the Prophet.
rows.anchor: { وإذ هم نجوى } أي متناجون في أمرك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Their whispered accusations included that he was mad, a magician, and bringing tales of the ancients.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: وكانت نجواهم قولهم إنه مجنون وإنه ساحر وإنه يأتي بأساطير الأولين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One occasion report says ʿUtba invited Quraysh notables to a meal; the Prophet recited to them and called them to God, prompting their whispered accusations.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت حين دعا عتبة أشراف قريش إلى طعام صنعه لهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says ʿAli prepared a meal for Quraysh chiefs at the Prophet’s order; after a call to monotheism they refused and whispered that he was bewitched.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عليا أن يتخذ طعاما ويدعو إليه أشراف قريش من المشركين

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains najwā as a verbal noun: they were people engaged in secret conversation.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: النجوى اسم للمصدر أي وإذ هم ذو نجوى، أي سرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “wrongdoers” were Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and their peers.
rows.anchor: أبو جهل والوليد بن المغيرة وأمثالهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called him bewitched in the sense of medically afflicted and mentally confused by magic, to drive people away from him.
rows.anchor: أي مطبوبا قد خبله السحر فاختلط عليه أمره، يقولون ذلك لينفروا عنه الناس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes “bewitched” to mean deceived, as in the question asking how people are deluded.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: «مسحورا» أي مخدوعا مثل قوله: فأنى تسحرون

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says masḥūr means having a lung: he needs food and drink and is an ordinary human, not an angel.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: «مسحورا» معناه أن له سحرا، أي رئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs describe a coward as having an inflated liver; masḥūr/masḥar also applies to any human or animal that eats or drinks.
rows.anchor: وتقول العرب للجبان: قد انتفخ سحره. ولكل من أكل من آدمي وغيره أو شرب مسحور ومسحر

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid’s verse uses masḥar for living beings sustained by food, supporting the lexical sense of eating and drinking.
rows.anchor: قال لبيد: فإن تسألينا فيم نحن فإننا عصافير من هذا الأنام المسحر

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays uses the verb for being fed and sustained by food and drink.
rows.anchor: وقال امرؤ القيس: أرانا موضعين لأمر غيب ونسحر بالطعام وبالشراب أي نغذى ونعلل

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha’s expression “between my liver and neck” is another attestation of the word’s bodily sense.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها قالت: من هذه التي تساميني من أزواج النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse marvels at their shifting descriptions of the Prophet as a magician, madman, and poet.
rows.anchor: عجبه من صنعهم كيف يقولون تارة ساحر وتارة مجنون وتارة شاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that they could find no stratagem to turn people away from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أي حيلة في صد الناس عنك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they strayed from truth and could find no route to guidance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ضلوا عن الحق فلا يجدون سبيلا، أي إلى الهدى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation is that their contradictions left them no way out of calling him mad, a magician, and a poet.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مخرجا لتناقض كلامهم في قولهم: مجنون، ساحر، شاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After hearing the Qur’an and its account of resurrection, they reasoned that an undeluded person would not make such a claim.
rows.anchor: قالوا وهم يتناجون لما سمعوا القرآن وسمعوا أمر البعث

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses rufāt as dust.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الرفات الغبار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses rufāt as soil.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: التراب

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والكسائي والفراء والأخفش
rows.claim: Rufāt means anything broken down and decayed, like crumbs, wreckage, or fragments; its verb means to crush.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة والكسائي والفراء والأخفش. تقول منه: رفت الشيء رفتا، أي حطم فهو مرفوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative is a denial, and khalqan is an accusative verbal noun meaning a new act of resurrection; this is the height of their rejection.
rows.anchor: «أئنا» استفهام والمراد به الجحد والإنكار. و«خلقا» نصب لأنه مصدر أي بعثا جديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to become stone or iron is a challenge intended to demonstrate their inability, even in hardness and strength.
rows.anchor: على جهة التعجيز حجارة أو حديدا في الشدة والقوة

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari’s challenge is: if they marvel at God making bones and flesh, they should become stone or iron if they can.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري: أي إن عجبتم من إنشاء الله لكم عظاما ولحما فكونوا أنتم حجارة أو حديدا إن قدرتم

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Even if they were stone or iron, they could not elude God when He wills them; the imperative is the strongest form of binding argument.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن عيسى: معناه أنكم لو كنتم حجارة أو حديدا لم تفوتوا الله عز وجل إذا أرادكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says that even if they were stone or iron, God would restore them as He first created them, then give them life after death.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لو كنتم حجارة أو حديدا لأعادكم كما بدأكم، ولأماتكم ثم أحياكم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the challenge means they may become whatever they wish, since they will still be restored.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: المعنى كونوا ما شئتم فستعادون

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas favors Mujahid’s reading: they acknowledge a Creator but deny resurrection, so even if they were stone or iron they would be raised as at first creation.
rows.anchor: النحاس: وهذا قول حسن لأنهم لا يستطيعون أن يكونوا حجارة، وإنما المعنى أنهم قد أقروا بخالقهم وأنكروا البعث

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: “Something greater in your hearts” means the heavens, earth, and mountains, whose vastness awes people; Qatada shares this sense.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: يعني السموات والأرض والجبال لعظمها في النفوس. وهو معنى قول قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this view, they may become anything, since God can cause them to die and then resurrect them.
rows.anchor: يقول: كونوا ما شئتم، فإن الله يميتكم ثم يبعثكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عمر وعبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص وابن جبير ومجاهد وعكرمة وأبو صالح والضحاك
rows.claim: These authorities say “something greater” is death, the greatest thing in a person’s mind; the verse means God can resurrect even those who became death.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وابن عمر وعبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص وابن جبير ومجاهد أيضا وعكرمة وأبو صالح والضحاك: يعني الموت

rows.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
rows.claim: Umayya’s verse witnesses that death is a terrifying creation in human hearts.
rows.anchor: قال أمية بن أبي الصلت: وللموت خلق في النفوس فظيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creative power that first originated them is the same power by which God brings them back.
rows.anchor: لأن القدرة التي بها أنشأتكم بها نعيدكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Death will appear on Judgment Day as a pale ram and be slaughtered between Paradise and the Fire.
rows.anchor: يؤتى بالموت يوم القيامة في صورة كبش أملح فيذبح بين الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the greatest thing in their hearts is resurrection itself.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد به البعث لأنه كان أكبر في صدورهم قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faṭarakum means that God created and originated them.
rows.anchor: { فطركم } خلقكم وأنشأكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They shake their heads mockingly; the verb is explained with its forms and with movement of the head.
rows.anchor: أي يحركون رؤوسهم استهزاء يقال: نغض رأسه ينغض وينغض نغضا ونغوضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rajaz line uses the verb for nodding the head toward someone.
rows.anchor: أنغض نحوي رأسه وأقنعا ويقال أيضا

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says the verb for moving one’s head can be transitive or intransitive; another verse uses it for teeth loosening and falling out.
rows.anchor: حكاه الأخفش. ويقال: نغضت سنه أي تحركت وانقلعت

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: A rajaz line describes teeth loosening with age.
rows.anchor: قال الراجز: ونغضت من هرم أسنانها

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A further poetic line attests to head movement at another’s sight.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر: لما رأتني أنغضت لي الرأسا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: Another line uses naghḍ for a waterwheel pulley and its movement.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر: لا ماء في المقراة إن لم تنهض بمسد فوق المحال النغض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When is it?” asks about the time of resurrection and return.
rows.anchor: { ويقولون متى هو } أي البعث والإعادة وهذا الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Perhaps it is near” means it is near, since ʿasā conveys certainty here and everything coming is near.
rows.anchor: { قل عسى أن يكون قريبا } أي هو قريب لأن عسى واجب نظيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call is a summons heard by all creatures to leave their graves and gather at the resurrection plain.
rows.anchor: الدعاء: النداء إلى المحشر بكلام تسمعه الخلائق، يدعوهم الله تعالى فيه بالخروج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the call is a blast they hear that summons them to assemble on the resurrection ground.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالصيحة التي يسمعونها فتكون داعية لهم إلى الاجتماع في أرض القيامة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report says people will be called on Judgment Day by their own and their fathers’ names, so they should choose good names.
rows.anchor: إنكم تدعون يوم القيامة بأسمائكم وأسماء آبائكم فأحسنوا أسماءكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They respond while acknowledging God’s right to praise for bringing them back to life.
rows.anchor: { فتستجيبون بحمده } أي باستحقاقه الحمد على الإحياء

rows.speaker: أبو سهل
rows.claim: Abu Sahl reads the phrase as “with praise to God,” supported by a poet’s use of the same construction.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سهل: أي والحمد لله كما قال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view is that they praise God aloud; Saʿid ibn Jubayr says unbelievers emerge saying “Glory and praise be to You,” though it will not benefit them then.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حامدين لله تعالى بألسنتكم. قال سعيد بن جبير: تخرج الكفار من قبورهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains “by His praise” as by His command, meaning they acknowledge Him as their Creator.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: «بحمده» بأمره أي تقرون بأنه خالقكم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains the response as coming through recognition and obedience to God.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: بمعرفته وطاعته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations are that the response is by God’s power or by His calling them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى بقدرته. وقيل: بدعائه إياكم

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: The scholars prefer that God’s true summons raises them: the trumpet is only a cause, and the resurrection day begins with praise and ends with it, as in the closing praise of 39:75.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا: وهو الصحيح فإن النفخ في الصور إنما هو سبب لخروج أهل القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their thinking they had stayed only a little may refer to the interval between the two blasts, when torment ceases for forty years and they sleep; this is specific to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: يعني بين النفختين وذلك أن العذاب يكف عن المعذبين بين النفختين، وذلك أربعون عاما

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says unbelievers get a spell of sleep before Judgment Day, then rise terrified when the graves are called.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: للكافرين هجعة قبل يوم القيامة يجدون فيها طعم النوم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says worldly life seems diminished when they see Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: المعنى أن الدنيا تحاقرت في أعينهم وقلت حين رأوا يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says they think they lived only a little in this world compared with their long stay in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: الحسن: «وتظنون إن لبثتم إلا قليلا» في الدنيا لطول لبثكم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported occasion is that an Arab insulted ʿUmar, who nearly killed him and risked stirring conflict; the verse then directed believers to speak best.
rows.anchor: والآية نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب. وذلك أن رجلا من العرب شتمه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Muslims asked permission to fight after prolonged abuse, but the Prophet said he had not yet been ordered to fight.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت لما قال المسلمون: ايذن لنا يا رسول الله في قتالهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The command may address people who recognize God as Creator while worshipping idols: they should use the best words of monotheism and prophetic confession.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى قل لعبادي الذين اعترفوا بأني خالقهم وهم يعبدون الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers debating unbelievers should use the best expression in affirming monotheism, as supported by the ban on insulting their deities.
rows.anchor: كما قال: { ولا تسبوا الذين يدعون من دون الله فيسبوا الله عدوا بغير علم }

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says that when an unbeliever speaks harshly, one should answer, “May God guide you” or “have mercy on you”; this was before fighting was prescribed.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو أن يقول للكافر إذا تشطط: هداك الله! يرحمك الله!

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes the command to enjoin what God ordered and forbid what He prohibited, applying to believers and unbelievers alike.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى قل لهم يأمروا بما أمر الله به وينهوا عما نهى الله عنه

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: A group restricts the command to believers among themselves: maintain good manners, gentle speech, humility, and avoid Satan’s provocations; the author calls this the best reading and says the verse remains operative.
rows.anchor: وقالت طائفة: أمر الله تعالى في هذه الآية المؤمنين فيما بينهم خاصة، بحسن الأدب وإلانة القول

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet’s command to be brothers supports the reading about courteous conduct among believers.
rows.anchor: وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan incites corruption and hostility between people; the discussion had appeared at the ends of al-Aʿraf and Yusuf.
rows.anchor: { إن الشيطان ينزغ بينهم } أي بالفساد وإلقاء العداوة والإغواء

rows.speaker: اليزيدي
rows.claim: Al-Yazidi explains nazagh as causing corruption between people.
rows.anchor: يقال: نزغ بيننا أي أفسد قاله اليزيدي

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another linguist glosses nazgh as incitement.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: النزغ الإغراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is openly and intensely hostile to humanity; this has also been stated in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: { إن الشيطان كان للإنسان عدوا مبينا } أي شديد العداوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes Satan failing to disrupt people remembering God when angels protected them, then stirring a nearby group into a quarrel and fight; the first group abandoned its gathering to reconcile them, to Satan’s delight.
rows.anchor: أن قوما جلسوا يذكرون الله عز وجل فجاء الشيطان ليقطع مجلسهم فمنعته الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Satan diverting the nearby group into a quarrel illustrates only one aspect of his enmity.
rows.anchor: فهذا من بعض عداوته

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj takes the address as directed to idolaters: God may guide them to Islam and show mercy, or let them die in idolatry and punish them.
rows.anchor: هذا خطاب للمشركين، والمعنى: إن يشأ يوفقكم للإسلام فيرحمكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here aʿlam is an intensive form meaning ʿalīm, just as akbar means kabīr.
rows.anchor: و «أعلم» بمعنى عليم نحو قولهم: الله أكبر، بمعنى كبير

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi offers an alternative address to believers: mercy means protection from Meccan unbelievers, while punishment means their being empowered over them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الخطاب للمؤمنين أي إن يشأ يرحكم بأن يحفظكم من كفار مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was not appointed to prevent their unbelief or make them believe; he is not their guarantor.
rows.anchor: أي وما وكلناك في منعهم من الكفر ولا جعلنا إليك إيمانهم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi also explains that the Prophet was not made responsible as their surety, answerable for them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما جعلناك كفيلا لهم تؤخذ بهم قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poet uses wakīl to mean guarantor or surety.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر: ذكرت أبا أروى فبت كأنني برد الأمور الماضيات وكيل أي كفيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed statement that God knows people establishes that He created them and made their characters, forms, conditions, and wealth diverse.
rows.anchor: أعاد بعد أن قال: { ربكم أعلم بكم } ليبين أنه خالقهم وأنه جعلهم مختلفين في أخلاقهم وصورهم وأحوالهم ومالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God likewise ranked the prophets according to His knowledge of their states; the discussion was treated in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وكذا النبيون فضل بعضهم على بعض عن علم منه بحالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Zabur is a scripture without legal rulings, duties, or legal limits, containing supplication, praise, and glorification.
rows.anchor: الزبور: كتاب ليس فيه حلال ولا حرام، ولا فرائض ولا حدود وإنما هو دعاء وتحميد وتمجيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God gave David the Zabur, He gave Muhammad the Qur’an; this answers the Jews’ argument.
rows.anchor: أي كما آتينا داود الزبور فلا تنكروا أن يؤتى محمد القرآن. وهو في محاجة اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Quraysh suffered drought and complained to the Prophet, God told them to call on those they worshipped as deities besides Him.
rows.anchor: لما ابتليت قريش بالقحط وشكوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنزل الله هذه الآية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the beings called upon are angels, Jesus, and Ezra.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: يعني الملائكة وعيسى وعزيرا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud says they are the jinn.
rows.anchor: ابن مسعود: يعني الجن

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the distress they cannot remove as the seven-year drought.
rows.anchor: أي القحط سبع سنين، على قول مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They can neither remove the distress nor transform it, such as changing poverty to wealth or sickness to health.
rows.anchor: من الفقر إلى الغنى ومن السقم إلى الصحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In one grammatical parsing, “those” is the subject, “who call” its adjective with an omitted object (“them”), and “seek” is the predicate or a circumstantial clause; another parsing makes “who call” the predicate.
rows.anchor: «أولئك» مبتدأ «الذين» صفة «أولئك» وضمير الصلة محذوف أي يدعونهم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud’s reading uses the second-person “you call”; the rest read the third-person “they call,” while everyone reads “they seek” in the third person.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود «تدعون» بالتاء على الخطاب. الباقون بالياء على الخبر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: In a report in Muslim, Ibn Masʿud says the verse concerns jinn who became Muslims although people had worshipped them, without knowing of their conversion.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم من كتاب التفسير عن عبد الله بن مسعود في قوله عز وجل

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: A variant of Ibn Masʿud’s report says Arab worshippers called on jinn who had become Muslim without the worshippers realizing it.
rows.anchor: في رواية قال: نزلت في نفر من العرب كانوا يعبدون نفرا من الجن

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi reports that the objects of worship were angels worshipped by some Arab tribes.
rows.anchor: ومنه أيضا أنهم الملائكة كانت تعبدهم قبائل من العرب ذكره الماوردي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid identify them as Ezra and Jesus.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد: عزير وعيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beings called upon seek nearness to God and supplicate Him for Paradise, which is the means of approach; this shows that the worshipped beings themselves seek nearness.
rows.anchor: و «يبتغون» يطلبون من الله الزلفة والقربة، ويتضرعون إلى الله تعالى في طلب الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “their Lord” may refer to worshippers, worshipped beings, or both; “they call” refers to worshippers while “they seek” refers to the worshipped.
rows.anchor: والهاء والميم في «ربهم» تعود على العابدين أو على المعبودين أو عليهم جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Which of them is nearer” can be a subject and predicate or a substitute for the pronoun in “they seek,” meaning each seeks the means to God according to nearness.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون «أيهم أقرب» بدلا من الضمير في «يبتغون»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They hope for God’s mercy and fear His punishment, which leaves no one secure and should be feared.
rows.anchor: إن عذاب ربك كان محذورا } أي مخوفا لا أمان لأحد منه

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Sahl says hope and fear are two states: when balanced a person’s affairs are sound, but if one outweighs the other its counterpart fails.
rows.anchor: وقال سهل بن عبد الله: الرجاء والخوف زمانان على الإنسان، فإذا استويا استقامت أحواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every town will be ruined before Judgment Day or subjected to severe punishment; “destroying” means ruining it.
rows.anchor: أي مخربوها

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the righteous town is ended by death and the wicked town by punishment.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: أما الصالحة فبالموت، وأما الطالحة فبالعذاب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud says that when fornication and usury appear in a town, God permits its destruction.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: إذا ظهر الزنى والربا في قرية أذن الله في هلاكهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One qualification is that the promise concerns an unjust town, supported by the statement that towns were destroyed only when their people were unjust; this warns unbelieving towns of punishment.
rows.anchor: فقيل: المعنى وإن من قرية ظالمة يقوي ذلك قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “Book” is the Preserved Tablet, and “inscribed” means written; satar is originally a verbal noun for writing.
rows.anchor: { كان ذلك في الكتاب } أي في اللوح. { مسطورا } أي مكتوبا. والسطر: الخط والكتابة

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarir’s verse uses the word satar for a line in a register.
rows.anchor: قال جرير: من شاء بايعته مالي وخلعته ما تكمل التيم في ديوانهم سطرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text gives the singular and plural forms of satar: asṭār, asāṭīr, asṭur, and sutūr.
rows.anchor: والسطر جمع أسطار مثل سبب وأسباب، ثم يجمع على أساطير

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن جريج وغيرهما
rows.claim: An ellipsis supplies “the signs they requested” and “lest they deny them and be destroyed,” which is why God withheld the requested signs.
rows.anchor: قال معناه قتادة وابن جريج وغيرهما. فأخر الله تعالى العذاب عن كفار قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God delayed punishment for Quraysh because He knew that some would believe and others would be born believers.
rows.anchor: لعلمه أن فيهم من يؤمن وفيهم من يولد مؤمنا

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: A report from al-Anʿam says Quraysh asked for Safa to become gold and mountains to move; Gabriel offered to grant it with immediate destruction if they disbelieved or to delay, and the Prophet chose delay.
rows.anchor: فنزل جبريل وقال: «إن شئت كان ما سأل قومك ولكنهم إن لم يؤمنوا لم يمهلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first “an” is accusative as the object of prevention, the second is nominative, and the bāʾ in “with the signs” is extra.
rows.anchor: و «أن» الأولى في محل نصب بوقوع المنع عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording that God was prevented is rhetorical emphasis: God cannot be prevented, but it means He does not send the signs, as though He were prevented.
rows.anchor: والله تعالى لا يكون ممنوعا عن شيء فالمعنى المبالغة في أنه لا يفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The she-camel was a bright, manifest sign proving Salih’s truth and God’s power.
rows.anchor: أي آية دالة مضيئة نيرة على صدق صالح، وعلى قدرة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud wronged the sign by denying it or rejecting that it came from God, so God destroyed them utterly.
rows.anchor: { فظلموا بها } أي ظلموا بتكذيبها. وقيل: جحدوا بها وكفروا أنها من عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five explanations of signs sent as warning are: prophetic lessons and miracles; signs of retribution warning against sin; life’s changes from childhood to old age (Ahmad ibn Hanbal); the Qur’an; and widespread death (al-Hasan).
rows.anchor: فيه خمسة أقوال: الأول العبر والمعجزات التي جعلها الله على أيدي الرسل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies “the people” as Meccans and God’s encompassing them as His promised destruction; past tense asserts its certainty, referring to Badr and the conquest.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الناس هنا أهل مكة، وإحاطته بهم إهلاكه إياهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن أبي نجيح
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Abi Najih take God’s encompassing as His power holding people in His grip, unable to escape His will.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد وابن أبي نجيح

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says God’s encompassing means His knowledge encompasses humanity.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: المعنى أحاط علمه بالناس

rows.speaker: الحسن وعروة وقتادة وغيرهم
rows.claim: Another view is God’s protection of the Prophet from being killed before delivering the message: his duty is to convey, and God protects him from the people.
rows.anchor: قال معناه الحسن وعروة وقتادة وغيرهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Bukhari and Tirmidhi, Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the vision as an actual sight the Prophet was shown on the night of the journey to Jerusalem, and the accursed tree as zaqqum; Tirmidhi grades the report sound.
rows.anchor: وفي البخاري والترمذي عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: عائشة ومعاوية والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك وابن أبي نجيح وابن زيد
rows.claim: These authorities share Ibn ʿAbbas’s interpretation of the vision and the accursed tree.
rows.anchor: وبقول ابن عباس قالت عائشة ومعاوية والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trial was that some converts apostatized when told the Prophet had traveled by night.
rows.anchor: وكانت الفتنة ارتداد قوم كانوا أسلموا حين أخبرهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه أسري به

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A dream interpretation is rejected because a dream would not be a trial and no one would deny it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانت رؤيا نوم. وهذه الآية تقضي بفساده، وذلك أن رؤيا المنام لا فتنة فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second Ibn ʿAbbas report identifies the vision as the Prophet dreaming that he would enter Mecca in the year of al-Hudaybiyya; his being turned back tried the Muslims, and he entered the following year.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال: الرؤيا التي في هذه الآية هي رؤيا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه يدخل مكة في سنة الحديبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The al-Hudaybiyya interpretation is weak because the sura is Meccan whereas that vision occurred in Medina.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا التأويل ضعف لأن السورة مكية وتلك الرؤيا كانت بالمدينة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third view says the Prophet dreamed the Umayyads would leap on his pulpit like monkeys; he grieved, then was told it was worldly rule given them and was comforted.
rows.anchor: وقال في رواية ثالثة: إنه عليه السلام رأى في المنام بني مروان ينزون على منبره نزو القردة

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: Sahl ibn Saʿd also says the vision concerned the Umayyads leaping on the pulpit like monkeys and grieving the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وهذا التأويل الثالث قاله أيضا سهل بن سعد رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: In his sermon concerning his pledge to Muʿawiya, al-Hasan ibn ʿAli recited that the vision might be a trial and temporary enjoyment.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن علي في خطبته في شأن بيعته لمعاوية

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya questions this reading and says it does not include ʿUthman, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, or Muʿawiya.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وفي هذا التأويل نظر، ولا يدخل في هذه الرؤيا عثمان ولا عمر بن عبد العزيز ولا معاوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase joins the Prophet’s vision and the accursed tree as two trials; their mention tested people through the threat of zaqqum.
rows.anchor: وفتنتها أنهم لما خوفوا بها قال أبو جهل استهزاء

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abu Jahl mocked the threat of a fire that burns stones yet supposedly grows trees, claiming zaqqum meant dates with butter, and served it to his companions.
rows.anchor: أبو جهل استهزاء: هذا محمد يتوعدكم بنار تحرق الحجارة، ثم يزعم أنها تنبت الشجر

rows.speaker: ابن الزبعرى
rows.claim: The same joke is attributed to Ibn al-Zibara, who said in Yemeni usage zaqqum means dates with butter; both may have said it.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: إن القائل ما نعلم الزقوم إلا التمر والزبد ابن الزبعرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mocking trial caused some weak believers to waver; the signs tested people so that those destined for disbelief disbelieved and those destined for faith affirmed.
rows.anchor: فافتتن أيضا لهذه المقالة بعض الضعفاء، فأخبر الله تعالى نبيه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: When told the Prophet claimed to have come from Jerusalem overnight, Abu Bakr said that if he said it, it was true, since he already trusted his revelation from heaven.
rows.anchor: إن كان قال ذلك فقد صدق

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq introduces the account of the night journey as collected from reports of Ibn Masʿud, Abu Saʿid, ʿAisha, Muʿawiya, al-Hasan, al-Zuhri, Qatada, and others, describing it as trial, proof, guidance, mercy, and confirmation for believers.
rows.anchor: قلت: ذكر هذا الخبر ابن إسحاق، ونصه: «قال كان من الحديث فيما بلغني عن مسراه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: In Ibn Ishaq’s report from Ibn Masʿud, the Prophet rode the Buraq, whose hoof reached the limit of sight, traveled to Jerusalem, met Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets, and led them in prayer.
rows.anchor: أتي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالبراق وهي الدابة التي كانت تحمل عليها الأنبياء

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: The Prophet was offered water, wine, and milk; a voice said water would drown him and his community, wine would lead them astray, and milk would guide them, so he drank milk and Gabriel affirmed their guidance.
rows.anchor: قال: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: فسمعت قائلا يقول حين عرضت علي إن أخذ الماء فغرق

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: In a report conveyed by Ibn Ishaq from al-Hasan, Gabriel woke the Prophet three times in the Hijr, then led him out to a white winged beast between a mule and donkey that carried him to Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: وحدثت عن الحسن أنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports from Qatada that the Buraq balked; Gabriel rebuked it, and it sweated with shame before settling for the Prophet to ride.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: وحدثت عن قتادة أنه قال: حدثت أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan’s account says the Prophet led the prophets in Jerusalem, chose milk rather than wine, and Gabriel said he had chosen the natural way and that wine was forbidden to his community.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن في حديثه: فمضى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومضى معه جبريل حتى انتهى إلى بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The Prophet returned to Mecca and reported the journey the next morning; many rejected it because a month-long caravan journey could not occur overnight, and many converts apostatized.
rows.anchor: فلما أصبح غدا على قريش فأخبرهم الخبر، فقال أكثر الناس: هذا والله الأمر البين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan’s account says Abu Bakr asked the Prophet to describe Jerusalem, confirmed each detail, testified that he was God’s Messenger, and was named al-Siddiq that day; the verse was revealed about those who apostatized.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «رفع لي حتى نظرت إليه» فجعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصفه لأبي بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report is al-Hasan’s account of the night journey incorporating Qatada’s report; remaining details are in the biography.
rows.anchor: فهذا حديث الحسن عن مسرى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وما دخل فيه من حديث قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the accursed tree is the Umayyads and that the Prophet exiled al-Hakam; the author calls this weak and novel, unlikely in a Meccan sura unless the verse were Medinan, which is unproven.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ضعيف محدث والسورة مكية، فيبعد هذا التأويل

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha told Marwan that God cursed his father while Marwan was still in his loins, so Marwan was part of the one cursed.
rows.anchor: وقد قالت عائشة لمروان: لعن الله أباك وأنت في صلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an does not curse the tree itself; it curses the unbelievers who eat it, so the phrase means the tree’s eaters are cursed.
rows.anchor: ولم يجز في القرآن لعن هذه الشجرة، ولكن الله لعن الكفار وهم آكلوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Arabs call harmful, repulsive food “accursed.”
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون هذا على قول العرب لكل طعام مكروه ضار: ملعون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another Ibn ʿAbbas interpretation identifies the tree as kashūth, a parasitic vine that coils around and kills trees.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الشجرة الملعونة هي هذه الشجرة التي تلتوي على الشجر فتقتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is by means of zaqqum, and their response to it only increases disbelief.
rows.anchor: { ونخوفهم } أي بالزقوم. { فما يزيدهم } التخويف إلا الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of Satan follows the warning that he is humanity’s enemy; it recalls his defiance as an example of the polytheists’ persistence against God.
rows.anchor: تقدم ذكر كون الشيطان عدو الإنسان، فانجر الكلام إلى ذكر آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Clay” means that Adam was created from clay, and Iblis’s question is one of denial.
rows.anchor: أي من طين. وهذا استفهام إنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation of Adam had been discussed in al-Baqara and al-Anʿam.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم القول في خلق آدم في «البقرة، والأنعام» مستوفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “Do You see?”, the k is an emphatic address; “this whom You honored” means the one You preferred over me.
rows.anchor: والكاف توكيد للمخاطبة. { هذا الذي كرمت علي } أي فضلته علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis considered the substance of fire superior to clay but did not know that the substances are alike.
rows.anchor: ورأى جوهر النار خيرا من جوهر الطين ولم يعلم أن الجواهر متماثلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This issue was previously discussed in al-Aʿraf.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم هذا في الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, “this” is the object of the verb and “who” its adjective; ikrām is a comprehensive name for all that is praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: و«هذا» نصب بأرأيت. «الذي» نعته. والإكرام: اسم جامع لكل ما يحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing supplies an ellipsis: “Tell me why You favored him over me, when You made me from fire and him from clay?”; the omitted words are understood.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف تقديره: أخبرني عن هذا الذي فضلته علي، لم فضلته وقد خلقتني من نار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, no ellipsis is needed: Iblis says, “Do You see this one You honored? I will do such-and-such to him.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا حاجة إلى تقدير الحذف، أي أترى هذا الذي كرمته علي لأفعلن به كذا وكذا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والفراء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Farraʾ gloss la-aḥtanikanna as “I will take control of them.”
rows.anchor: في قول ابن عباس: لأستولين عليهم. وقاله الفراء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses it as “I will encompass them.”
rows.anchor: مجاهد: لأحتوينهم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses it as “I will lead them astray.”
rows.anchor: ابن زيد: لأضلنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These explanations converge on Iblis overwhelming Adam’s descendants through misguidance and seduction.
rows.anchor: والمعنى متقارب، أي لأستأصلن ذريته بالإغواء والإضلال، ولأجتاحنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs say locusts “consume” a crop when they take all of it; another possible sense is to drive people wherever one wishes with a bridle, as with a horse.
rows.anchor: وروي عن العرب: احتنك الجراد الزرع إذا ذهب به كله

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poetic line uses the verb for a year that exhausted people and consumed their wealth.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر: أشكو إليك سنة قد أجحفت جهدا إلى جهد بنا وأضعفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Except a few” means those protected from Satan, identified as God’s servants in 17:65.
rows.anchor: يعني المعصومين، وهم الذين ذكرهم الله في قوله: { إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis made a conjecture, knew the human tendency to desire, or inferred vulnerability from the angels’ statement about corruption on earth.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال إبليس ذلك ظنا، كما قال الله تعالى: { ولقد صدق عليهم إبليس ظنه }

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Iblis expected this because he tempted Adam and found him without resolve.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: ظن ذلك لأنه وسوس إلى آدم عليه السلام فلم يجد له عزما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Go” is a command of humiliation: strive as hard as you can, for God has granted you respite.
rows.anchor: هذا أمر إهانة، أي اجهد جهدك فقد أنظرناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who follow Satan are the descendants of Adam who obey him.
rows.anchor: { فمن تبعك } أي أطاعك من ذرية آدم

rows.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
rows.claim: The recompense is abundant; the word is an accusative verbal noun from a root used transitively and intransitively.
rows.anchor: أي وافرا، عن مجاهد وغيره. وهو نصب على المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istifzāz means to make someone slip or lightly unsettle him; its root means cutting, as in a garment coming apart, and it can describe fear making someone unsteady.
rows.anchor: أي استزل واستخف، وأصله القطع، ومنه تفزز الثوب إذا انقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative is a challenge: Satan cannot mislead anyone or hold authority over anyone, so he is told to do what he can.
rows.anchor: «واستفزز» أمر تعجيز، أي أنت لا تقدر على إضلال أحد، وليس لك على أحد سلطان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Satan’s voice is every caller who invites someone to disobey God.
rows.anchor: وصوته كل داع يدعو إلى معصية الله تعالى، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies Satan’s voice as singing, instruments, and amusement.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: الغناء والمزامير واللهو

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies Satan’s voice as the flute.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: صوت المزمار

rows.speaker: الغزنوي
rows.claim: Al-Ghaznawi tells that Satan played music between the descendants of Habil and Qabil, drawing men from the mountain to beautiful women and leading them to fornication.
rows.anchor: ذكره الغزنوي. وقيل: «بصوتك» بوسوستك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes Satan’s voice as his whispering.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «بصوتك» بوسوستك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijlāb originally means driving with a clamor; here it means gathering every scheme Satan can muster against them.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أجمع عليهم كلما تقدر عليه من مكايدك

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes take Satan’s cavalry and foot soldiers as every rider or walker acting in disobedience to God.
rows.anchor: وقال أكثر المفسرين: يريد كل راكب وماش في معصية الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, and Qatada say Satan has mounted and foot troops from jinn and humans, meaning anyone riding or walking in disobedience.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة: إن له خيلا ورجلا من الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says a horse used in sin, a person walking in sin, illicit wealth, and a child of fornication all belong to Satan.
rows.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد عن ابن عباس قال: كل خيل سارت في معصية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajil is the plural of rāجل, just as ṣaḥb is plural of ṣāḥib.
rows.anchor: والرجل جمع راجل، مثل صحب وصاحب

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs reads rajlik with kasra on the jīm; it is one of two dialect forms meaning “walker.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص «ورجلك» بكسر الجيم وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: عكرمة وقتادة
rows.claim: Ikrima and Qatada read rajālik in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة وقتادة «ورجالك» على الجمع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Satan’s share in wealth is spending it in disobedience.
rows.anchor: فشركته في الأموال إنفاقها في معصية الله، قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Satan’s share in wealth is property acquired unlawfully.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي التي أصابوها من غير حلها، قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatada say it includes the forbidden livestock categories called baḥīra, sāʾiba, waṣīla, and ḥām.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: ما كانوا يحرمونه من البحيرة والسائبة والوصيلة والحام. وقاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says Satan’s share in wealth includes animals sacrificed to idols.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: ما كانوا يذبحونه لآلهتهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك وعبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and Ibn ʿAbbas say Satan’s share in children includes those born through fornication.
rows.anchor: قيل: هم أولاد الزنى، قاله مجاهد والضحاك وعبد الله بن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another Ibn ʿAbbas interpretation includes killing children and other crimes committed against them.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا هو ما قتلوا من أولادهم وأتوا فيهم من الجرائم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another interpretation is naming children after idols or spirits, such as ʿAbd al-Harith, ʿAbd al-ʿUzza, and ʿAbd al-Lat.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا: هو تسميتهم عبد الحارث وعبد العزى وعبد اللات وعبد الشمس ونحوه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Satan shares children by their parents’ raising them in unbelief, such as Christians baptizing their children.
rows.anchor: كصنع النصارى بأولادهم بالغمس في الماء الذي لهم، قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A fifth view from Mujahid says that if a man has intercourse without invoking God, a jinn joins him, as in the description of Paradise’s women untouched by human or jinn.
rows.anchor: وقول خامس روي عن مجاهد قال: إذا جامع الرجل ولم يسم انطوى الجان على إحليله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from ʿAisha says the Prophet explained “those shared by jinn” as people whose lineage includes jinn; al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim records it in Nawadir al-Usul.
rows.anchor: وروي من حديث عائشة قالت قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن فيكم مغربين

rows.speaker: الهروي
rows.claim: Al-Harawi says they are called mughrabūn because a foreign lineage entered their ancestry.
rows.anchor: قال الهروي: سموا مغربين لأنه دخل فيهم عرق غريب

rows.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim says jinn can resemble Adam’s descendants in matters and intermix with them; he says one of Bilqis’s parents was jinn.
rows.anchor: قال الترمذي الحكيم: فللجن مساماة بابن آدم في الأمور والاختلاط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan promises false hopes: no resurrection or judgment, or that his followers would be especially entitled to Paradise; this is supported by 4:120.
rows.anchor: أي منهم الأماني الكاذبة، وأنه لا قيامة ولا حساب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view is that Satan promises victory over anyone who wants to harm them; the command is a threat to Satan and contempt for him and his followers.
rows.anchor: وقيل «وعدهم» أي عدهم النصرة على من أرادهم بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Mujahid’s interpretation of Satan’s voice as singing and instruments, the verse indicates their prohibition; everything that is Satan’s voice, action, or pleasure must be avoided.
rows.anchor: في الآية ما يدل على تحريم المزامير والغناء واللهو

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Nafiʿ reports that Ibn ʿUmar heard a shepherd’s flute, plugged his ears, and turned his mount aside; he restored his hands and route when it could no longer be heard, saying he had seen the Prophet do likewise.
rows.anchor: وروى نافع عن ابن عمر أنه سمع صوت زمارة فوضع أصبعيه في أذنيه

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: The scholars argue that if this was their response to a moderate sound, one should be even more cautious of contemporary singing and instruments; fuller discussion will come in Luqman.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا: إذا كان هذا فعلهم في حق صوت لا يخرج عن الاعتدال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies God’s servants whom Satan cannot control as the believers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هم المؤمنون وقد تقدم الكلام فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is their protector, preserving them from accepting Satan’s tricks and evil schemes.
rows.anchor: أي عاصما من القبول من إبليس، وحافظا من كيده وسوء مكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Izjāʾ means to drive or propel, as in God driving clouds in 24:43.
rows.anchor: الإزجاء: السوق، ومنه قوله تعالى: { ألم تر أن الله يزجي سحابا }

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poetic address to a rider uses muzjī for one who drives his mount.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر: يأيها الراكب المزجي مطيته سائل بني أسد ما هذه الصوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Propelling ships means moving them with a gentle wind; fulk is a plural, as discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: وإزجاء الفلك: سوقه بالريح اللينة. والفلك هنا جمع، وقد تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea is a great body of water, fresh or salty, though common usage associates the name with salt water.
rows.anchor: والبحر الماء الكثير عذبا كان أو ملحا، وقد غلب هذا الاسم على المشهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse recalls God’s favors so people will not associate partners with Him.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية توقيف على آلاء الله وفضله عند عباده، أي ربكم الذي أنعم عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God’s bounty means engaging in trade; He is merciful to them.
rows.anchor: { لتبتغوا من فضله } أي في التجارات. وقد تقدم. { إنه كان بكم رحيما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harm in the sea includes fear of drowning, being unable to sail, and the turbulence and surging of the water.
rows.anchor: «الضر» لفظ يعم خوف الغرق والإمساك عن الجري. وأهوال حالاته اضطرابه وتموجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “All but Him are lost” means the idols perish and is a contemptuous way of describing false deities.
rows.anchor: «ضل» معناه تلف وفقد، وهي عبارة تحقير لمن يدعي إلها من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists imagine their idols intercede, yet innate knowledge tells them idols are powerless in great calamities; the sea confronts them with a state where means fail.
rows.anchor: أن الكفار إنما يعتقدون في أصنامهم أنها شافعة، وأن لها فضلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once saved to land, they turn away from sincere devotion to God.
rows.anchor: { فلما نجاكم إلى البر أعرضتم } أي عن الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The human being” can mean an unbeliever, or humanity in general as naturally ungrateful for blessings except those God protects.
rows.anchor: الإنسان هنا الكافر. وقيل: وطبع الإنسان كفورا للنعم إلا من عصمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning shows God can destroy people on land even after sparing them at sea.
rows.anchor: بين أنه قادر على هلاكهم في البر وإن سلموا من البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khasf means the earth caves in beneath something; the text gives related uses for a collapsed well, a sunken eye, a dried spring, and the sun setting.
rows.anchor: والخسف: أن تنهار الأرض بالشيء، يقال: بئر خسيف إذا انهدم أصلها

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr says khasīf is a well dug into rock whose abundant water does not run out; its plural is khusf.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: والخسيف البئر التي تحفر في الحجارة فلا ينقطع ماؤها كثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “side of the land” is called a side because it becomes one after collapse, and because sea and land are each a side.
rows.anchor: وسماه جانبا لأنه يصير بعد الخسف جانبا. وأيضا فإن البحر جانب والبر جانب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: They were on the seashore, safe from the sea’s danger, so God warned them of danger on the land they considered safe as well as of danger at sea.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهم كانوا على ساحل البحر، وساحله جانب البر، وكانوا فيه آمنين من أهوال البحر

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والقتبي
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda and al-Qutaybi say a ḥāṣib is a fierce wind that hurls small stones.
rows.anchor: يعني ريحا شديدة، وهي التي ترمي بالحصباء، وهي الحصى الصغار، قاله أبو عبيدة والقتبي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the warning may mean stones raining from the sky, as happened to Lot’s people.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: يعني حجارة من السماء تحصبهم، كما فعل بقوم لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cloud that throws hail can be called ḥāṣib; a wind carrying dust and gravel is also ḥāṣib or ḥaṣiba.
rows.anchor: ويقال للسحابة التي ترمي بالبرد: حاصب، وللريح التي تحمل التراب والحصباء حاصب وحصبة أيضا

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid’s line describes a violent wind sweeping over abandoned homes.
rows.anchor: قال لبيد: جرت عليها أن خوت من أهلها أذيالها كل عصوف حصبه

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s line uses ḥāṣib for wind scattering something like cotton fluff.
rows.anchor: وقال الفرزدق: مستقبلين شمال الشام يضربنا بحاصب كنديف القطن منثور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wakīl here is a protector or supporter who could shield them from God’s force.
rows.anchor: أي حافظا ونصيرا يمنعكم من بأس الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Return you to it another time” means returning them to the sea.
rows.anchor: يعني في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāṣif is a fierce, destructive wind named from breaking; the passage lists related senses of crushing, loud thunder, brittle wood, and amusement as a later usage.
rows.anchor: القاصف: الريح الشديدة التي تكسر بشدة من قصف الشيء يقصفه أي كسره بشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Because of your disbelief” means on account of your disbelief.
rows.anchor: { فيغرقكم بما كفرتم } أي بكفركم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read the five verbs “make sink,” “send,” “return,” “send,” and “drown” with nūn, the first-person plural of majesty.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو، «نخسف بكم» «أو نرسل عليكم» «أن نعيدكم» «فنرسل عليكم» «فنغرقكم» بالنون في الخمسة

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use yāʾ in those verbs, matching the earlier reference to God as “Him.”
rows.anchor: الباقون بالياء لقوله في الآية قبل: «إياه»

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة ورويس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, Ruways, and Mujahid read “so it drowns you” with tāʾ, referring to the wind.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة ورويس ومجاهد «فتغرقكم» بالتاء نعتا للريح

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada read the verb with yāʾ and a doubled rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن وقتادة «فيغرقكم» بالياء مع التشديد في الراء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads the plural “winds” here and throughout the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر «الرياح» هنا وفي كل القرآن

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi reports that qāṣif is the wind that destroys on land, while ʿāṣif is the wind that sinks at sea.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن القاصف المهلكة في البر، والعاصف المغرقة في البحر حكاه الماوردي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses tabīʿ as an avenger; al-Nahhas relates the word to vengeance and also to one who pursues a claim, as in the legal phrase in 2:178.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: ثائرا. النحاس: وهو من الثأر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After warnings, the verse also sets out God’s blessings on humanity.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر من الترهيب ما ذكر بين النعمة عليهم أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled verb karramnā means granting nobility and distinction, not wealth.
rows.anchor: «كرمنا» تضعيف كرم أي جعلنا لهم كرما أي شرفا وفضلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human honor includes upright stature and good form, deliberate transport over land and sea, and special provision of foods, drink, and clothing; humans earn wealth and prepare composite dishes unlike other animals.
rows.anchor: وهذه الكرامة يدخل فيها خلقهم على هذه الهيئة في امتداد القامة وحسن الصورة

rows.speaker: جماعة
rows.claim: A group cited by al-Tabari says the distinction is that humans eat with their hands while other animals eat with their mouths.
rows.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن جماعة أن التفضيل هو أن يأكل بيده وسائر الحيوان بالفم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil also give eating with the hand as the distinction.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الكلبي ومقاتل ذكره الماوردي

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says humanity was honored with speech and discernment.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: كرمهم بالنطق والتمييز

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAta says humanity was honored with balanced, extended stature.
rows.anchor: عطاء: كرمهم بتعديل القامة وامتدادها

rows.speaker: يمان
rows.claim: Yaman says humanity was honored with beautiful form.
rows.anchor: يمان: بحسن الصورة

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says humanity was honored by having Muhammad among them.
rows.anchor: محمد بن كعب: بأن جعل محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم

rows.speaker: محمد بن جرير الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says humanity was distinguished by dominion over other creatures and their subjection to people.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن جرير الطبري: بتسليطهم على سائر الخلق، وتسخير سائر الخلق لهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other views identify speech and writing, or understanding and discernment, as the distinction.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالكلام والخط. وقيل: بالفهم والتمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author’s preferred basis of human distinction is reason, the foundation of moral responsibility: through it people know God, understand revelation, reach bliss, and affirm messengers; because reason alone is insufficient, God sent messengers and books. He compares law to the sun and reason to the eye.
rows.anchor: والصحيح الذي يعول عليه أن التفضيل إنما كان بالعقل الذي هو عمدة التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some animals surpass humans in particular traits, such as a horse’s speed, an elephant’s strength, a lion’s courage, and a rooster’s noble bearing, but humanity’s central distinction is reason.
rows.anchor: وقد جعل الله في بعض الحيوان خصالا يفضل بها ابن آدم أيضا كجري الفرس وسمعه وإبصاره

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: A group argues that the verse implies angels outrank humans and jinn because 4:172 exempts the nearest angels from servitude.
rows.anchor: ولا الملائكة المقربون [النساء: 171]. وهذا غير لازم من الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inference is not necessary: this verse compares people with animals and perhaps jinn, whereas angels lie outside the group under discussion; it leaves open whether angels are better, worse, or equal.
rows.anchor: وهذا غير لازم من الآية، بل التفضيل فيها بين الإنس والجن

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some avoid discussing whether angels outrank humans or whether prophets outrank one another, citing a report not to compare prophets or prefer the Prophet to Jonah.
rows.anchor: وقد تحاشى قوم من الكلام في هذا كما تحاشوا من الكلام في تفضيل بعض الأنبياء على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report is not a sound basis for silence, since the Qur’an explicitly ranks prophets; the matter was discussed in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وهذا ليس بشيء لوجود النص في القرآن في التفضيل بين الأنبياء

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says “wholesome things” are tasty foods such as ghee, honey, butter, dates, and sweets, while other creatures subsist on fodder and bones.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: السمن والعسل والزبد والتمر والحلوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human superiority over beasts, livestock, wild animals, and birds includes mastery, reward, protection, discernment, and insight.
rows.anchor: أي على البهائم والدواب والوحش والطير بالغلبة والاستيلاء، والثواب والجزاء والحفظ والتمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes a report attributed to ʿAisha that one should deprive oneself of tasty food because Satan runs through the veins with its strength; the author says it has no basis and authentic Sunnah contradicts it.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية ترد ما روي عن عائشة رضي الله عنها

rows.speaker: الصوفية
rows.claim: Some Sufis use that report to justify avoiding wholesome foods.
rows.anchor: وبه يستدل كثير من الصوفية في ترك أكل الطيبات

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Tusi relates that Sahl lived for a period on nabq leaves and spent three years eating thin fig leaves.
rows.anchor: وقد حكى أبو حامد الطوسي قال: كان سهل يقتات ورق النبق مدة

rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn al-Banna relates that Dhu al-Nun refused a companion’s salt and bread, saying the finely ground salt would prevent success, and subsisted on a little barley meal.
rows.anchor: وذكر إبراهيم بن البنا قال: صحبت ذا النون من إخميم إلى الإسكندرية

rows.speaker: أبو يزيد
rows.claim: Abu Yazid says he ate none of the food other people eat for forty years.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو يزيد: ما أكلت شيئا مما يأكله بنو آدم أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: The scholars say such self-imposed deprivation should not be practiced: God honored humans with wheat and reserved its husks for livestock, and subsisting on bran competes with animals; barley and coarse salt can harm health, while refusing suitable food opposes divine wisdom, law, and reason. The body is a mount that must be cared for.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا: وهذا مما لا يجوز حمل النفس عليه لأن الله تعالى أكرم الآدمي بالحنطة

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Adham ate butter, honey, and fine bread, saying that when they had food they ate like men and when they lacked it they endured like men.
rows.anchor: وروي عن إبراهيم بن أدهم أنه اشترى زبدا وعسلا وخبز حوارى

rows.speaker: الثوري
rows.claim: Al-Thawri ate meat, grapes, and fālūdhaj, then rose to pray; similar examples from the early Muslims are numerous.
rows.anchor: وكان الثوري يأكل اللحم والعنب والفالوذج ثم يقوم إلى الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls the reported ascetic deprivation an excess in religion, if the reports are sound, and links it to the statement that monasticism was invented rather than prescribed.
rows.anchor: ورهبانية ابتدعوها ما كتبناها عليهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra describes the blessed person receiving a book in the right hand, growing sixty cubits tall, having a bright face and pearl crown, and being welcomed by companions; the condemned person is dark-faced, equally tall, and rejected by companions. Al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan gharīb.
rows.anchor: روى الترمذي عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering of every community is like the scene in 45:28, when each nation kneels and is called to its record.
rows.anchor: وترى كل أمة جاثية كل أمة تدعى إلى كتابها اليوم تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A record is called an imam because people return to it to learn what they did.
rows.anchor: والكتاب يسمى إماما لأنه يرجع إليه في تعرف أعمالهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak say each person is summoned with his own record of deeds, supported by the following phrase about receiving the book in the right hand.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والضحاك: «بإمامهم» أي بكتابهم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says people are summoned by the revealed scripture they followed: Torah adherents by Torah and Qur’an adherents by Qur’an, then asked whether they obeyed its commands and avoided its prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: بالكتاب المنزل عليهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says each group is summoned with its prophet, the leader it followed, including followers of Abraham, Moses, Satan, and idols; the righteous take their records in the right hand and the false in the left.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: «بإمامهم» بنبيهم، والإمام من يؤتم به

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada also transmits the view that people are summoned according to the prophet or leader they followed.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: «بإمامهم» بنبيهم، والإمام من يؤتم به

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAli says they are called by the imam of their era.
rows.anchor: وقال علي رضي الله عنه: بإمام عصرهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report says everyone is called by the leader of their time, God’s Book, and their prophet’s Sunnah, with groups summoned by their prophets or by Satan and misguided leaders.
rows.anchor: كل يدعى بإمام زمانهم وكتاب ربهم وسنة نبيهم فيقول هاتوا متبعي إبراهيم

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو العالية وابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu al-ʿAliya, and Ibn ʿAbbas interpret “their imam” as their deeds, so people are called by their accepted or forbidden conduct.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وأبو العالية: «بإمامهم» أي بأعمالهم. وقاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Another interpretation, identified with Abu ʿUbayda, is that people are called by the religious school they followed, such as Hanafi, Shafiʿi, Muʿtazili, or Qadari.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بمذاهبهم فيدعون بمن كانوا يأتمون به في الدنيا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says people of charity are called from the gate of charity and people of jihad from the gate of jihad.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة: يدعى أهل الصدقة من باب الصدقة، وأهل الجهاد من باب الجهاد

rows.speaker: أبو سهل
rows.claim: Abu Sahl says people are called by their known deeds, such as the prayerful and fasting, or in blame such as tale-bearers and gossips.
rows.anchor: أبو سهل: يقال أين فلان المصلي والصوام، وعكسه الدفاف والنمام

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says they are called by their mothers.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: «بإمامهم» بأمهاتهم

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: The philosophers explain calling people by their mothers in three ways: to account for Jesus, to honor al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and to conceal the parentage of illegitimate children.
rows.anchor: قالت الحكماء: وفي ذلك ثلاثة أوجه من الحكمة أحدهما لأجل عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The maternal-name view is doubtful because the sound report says every betrayer will be identified by his own and his father’s name, which contradicts the claim that maternal names conceal fathers.
rows.anchor: فإن في الحديث الصحيح عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Whoever receives his book in his right hand” reinforces the interpretation of imam as the record, as does 36:12.
rows.anchor: { فمن أوتي كتابه بيمينه } هذا يقوي قول من قال: «بإمامهم» بكتابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fatīl is the thread in the cleft of a date stone; the discussion appeared in al-Nisaʾ.
rows.anchor: الفتيل الذي في شق النواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blindness here means being blind in worldly life to reflection and seeing the truth, and blind in the afterlife concerning its affairs.
rows.anchor: أي في الدنيا عن الاعتبار وإبصار الحق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When people from Yemen asked Ibn ʿAbbas about the verse, he directed them to the preceding passage about God’s blessings and ships; one blind to those worldly signs is even more astray about the unseen afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: من كان في هذه النعم والآيات التي رأى أعمى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that whoever is blind to God’s worldly favors will be blind to the favors of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى من عمي عن النعم التي أنعم الله بها عليه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view contrasts the worldly life, where one has respite and promised acceptance of repentance, with the afterlife, where repentance is unavailable.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى من كان في الدنيا التي أمهل فيها وفسح له ووعد بقبول التوبة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says an unbeliever or astray person in worldly life will be more blind and astray in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: من كان في هذه الدنيا كافرا ضالا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says whoever is blind to God’s proofs in this life will be raised blind on Judgment Day, as in 20:124 and 17:97.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من كان في الدنيا أعمى عن حجج الله بعثه الله يوم القيام أعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across the interpretations, “more blind” describes intensified blindness of the heart, unlike physical blindness of the eye.
rows.anchor: في جميع الأقوال: أشد عمى لأنه من عمى القلب، ولا يقال مثله في عمى العين

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh say the comparative form is not used for bodily defects treated as innate traits, like a hand or leg; hence one does not say “how blind” or “how handed.”
rows.anchor: قال الخليل وسيبويه: لأنه خلقة بمنزلة اليد والرجل

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says that comparative form is not used because the word exceeds three letters, although some grammarians allow it since the verbs are ʿamiya and ʿashiya.
rows.anchor: الأخفش: لم يقل فيه ذلك لأنه على أكثر من ثلاثة أحرف

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ reports hearing Arabs say “how black his hair is,” and cites poetry using comparative color forms.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: حدثني بالشأم شيخ بصرى أنه سمع العرب تقول: ما أسود شعره

rows.speaker: أبو بكر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Abu Bakr, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Khalaf use imāla on both occurrences of aʿmā; Abu ʿAmr uses it on the first only, while the others open both.
rows.anchor: وأمال أبو بكر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف الحرفين «أعمى» و«أعمى»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “More astray in way” means the person finds no route to guidance.
rows.anchor: { وأضل سبيلا } يعني أنه لا يجد طريقا إلى الهداية

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says Quraysh stopped the Prophet touching the Black Stone unless he touched their idols; he considered a slight concession, but God prevented it and revealed the verse, as reported by Mujahid and Qatada.
rows.anchor: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يستلم الحجر الأسود في طوافه، فمنعته قريش

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, via ʿAta, says a Thaqif delegation asked to keep their idols for a year to collect gifts, then break them and convert, while their valley received Mecca’s sanctuary status; the Prophet nearly granted this before the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: نزلت في وفد ثقيف، أتوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فسألوه شططا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says Quraysh chiefs asked the Prophet to dismiss poor clients so they could listen with him; he nearly did so but was forbidden.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو قول أكابر قريش للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: اطرد عنا هؤلاء السقاط والموالي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Quraysh privately flattered and honored the Prophet all night, almost persuading him to accommodate part of their request, until God protected him and revealed the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: ذكر لنا أن قريشا خلوا برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات ليلة إلى الصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaftinunaka means to remove or divert someone from his position; here they sought to turn the Prophet from the Qur’an’s ruling, since their proposed concession contradicted it.
rows.anchor: { ليفتنونك } أي يزيلونك. يقال: فتنت الرجل عن رأيه إذا أزلته عما كان عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “To invent something else against Us” refers to fabricating a revelation that sanctified Thaqif’s valley, trees, birds, and game so the Prophet could claim God had ordered it.
rows.anchor: أي لتختلق علينا غير ما أوحينا إليك، وهو قول ثقيف: وحرم وادينا كما حرمت مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had he yielded, they would have taken him as an intimate friend, allied and reconciled to him for his accommodation.
rows.anchor: أي والوك وصافوك مأخوذ من الخلة بالضم وهي الصداقة لممايلته لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lexical alternative derives khalīl from khulla, poverty: they would have made him needy through his dependence on them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «لاتخذوك خليلا» أي فقيرا. مأخوذ من الخلة بفتح الخاء وهي الفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God kept the Prophet firm in truth and protected him from agreeing with them; r-k-n means to lean, and “a little” means slight inclination.
rows.anchor: أي على الحق وعصمناك من موافقتهم. { لقد كدت تركن إليهم } أي تميل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says that after this verse the Prophet prayed, “O God, do not leave me to myself for even a blink.”
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: لما نزلت هذه الآية قال عليه السلام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes the outward address as to the Prophet but its inward meaning as a statement about Thaqif: they nearly claimed he leaned toward them, attributing their action to him by figurative extension.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ظاهر الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وباطنه إخبار عن ثقيف

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri denies that the Prophet actually inclined toward them: without God’s grace he might have leaned toward agreement, but God’s favor ensured he did not.
rows.anchor: بل المعنى: ولولا فضل الله عليك لكان منك ميل إلى موافقتهم، ولكن تم فضل الله عليك فلم تفعل ذكره القشيري

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the Prophet was protected from error; the passage instructs the community not to accommodate polytheists in God’s rulings and laws.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم معصوما، ولكن هذا تعريف للأمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, and others say the hypothetical doubled punishment would mean twice the torment of worldly life and twice the torment after death; this is an ultimate threat, and the higher the rank, the graver the penalty for disobedience.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما. وهذا غاية الوعيد. وكلما كانت الدرجة أعلى كان العذاب عند المخالفة أعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍiʿf can mean twice the amount, or a share as in “for each a share,” with the discussion treated earlier in al-Aʿraf.
rows.anchor: وضعف الشيء مثله مرتين وقد يكون الضعف النصيب كقوله عز وجل: «لكل ضعف»
